title: Keep every wagon's _features.yaml listing every feature module with its current status

facts.note: Trigger hint: task text mentions a wagon or its features. Applicability itself is unconditional for every wagon; this fact only helps decide when to check.
Trigger hint: a wagon features manifest is touched. The source supplies no directory layout, so this glob does not by itself prove every wagon is covered.
Trigger hint: needs a diff-level observer comparing a wagon's feature modules against its _features.yaml entries.
Needs an observer that compares any wagon's feature modules and actual states with its manifest, independent of what the current edit touched.

fires: Any wagon exists whose _features.yaml omits one of its feature modules or carries a status that is not current, regardless of what edit surfaced it.
A planner adds, removes, renames or changes the status of a feature module in a wagon.
A planner creates or edits a wagon's _features.yaml or other wagon plan artifacts.
A planner's work (including edits to feature internals, code or tests) reveals that a wagon's manifest is incomplete or stale.
doesNotFire: Work that concerns no wagon at all (no wagon, feature module or features manifest is involved or affected).

given: Any wagon and its _features.yaml (the features manifest)
when: The planner authors, updates or relies on that wagon's plan artifacts, or finds the manifest out of step with the wagon's feature modules
then: The wagon's _features.yaml lists every feature module of the wagon together with its current status.
prefer: Update _features.yaml in the same change that adds, removes, renames or re-statuses a feature module.
Treat _features.yaml as the wagon's single index of feature modules and statuses.
Correct an existing omission or stale status when you encounter it, even if your triggering edit was elsewhere.
avoid: Feature modules that exist under the wagon but are missing from _features.yaml.
Entries whose status is stale or no longer matches the feature's actual state.
Entries for feature modules that no longer exist.
why: The features manifest is the wagon's index of its feature modules and statuses; feature registration and wagon-feature coverage checks read it, so an incomplete or stale manifest breaks them.
evidence: Every feature module under the wagon has a matching entry in its _features.yaml, and every entry corresponds to an existing feature module.
Each entry carries a status that reflects the feature's current state.
verifier_detail: Term features_manifest: the wagon's _features.yaml index of feature modules + statuses.
